items.caption: An oracle-script form labeled 好, with a compact 女-like figure above a larger 子-like figure. Early forms are analyzed as 女 plus 子, though their proposed mother–child meaning is not directly attested in the cited uses.
items.alt: Black glyph with a compact looped upper figure and a broader, angular lower figure.
items.selection_reason: The visible arrangement makes the proposed 女-plus-子 analysis easier to discuss while leaving the graph’s original motivation open.

items.caption: A bronze-script form labeled 好, with a distinct upper figure and a broad lower element. Early forms could vary in the placement of 女 and 子; this example does not by itself establish a sequence of change.
items.alt: Black glyph with a tall left figure and a rounded, open right-hand form.
items.selection_reason: Adds a visually different early form relevant to reported graphic variation; its appearance alone does not identify the elements or establish chronology.

limitations.text: The early graph is analyzed as 女 plus 子, and a mother–child affection interpretation is favored by some accounts, but cited early uses do not directly attest that meaning. Other proposed motivations remain unresolved.

These are modern vector redrawings labeled by script tradition, not photographs of inscribed artifacts. The selected forms illustrate candidates rather than a securely established chronological sequence.
